findings.title: Device limit bypassed because rejected devices are cached as already tagged
findings.body:
`tagDeviceUI` writes the device key into `localCache` (29-minute TTL) before calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice`. When the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the key stays cached.

The device's next request hits the cache, `tagDeviceUI` returns nil, and `Anonymous.Authenticate` grants access. The limit is enforced only on the first request from a new device; a reload or retry gets in.

The same ordering means a transient DB error suppresses re-tagging for 29 minutes. Fix: on `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, cache a negative marker and return the error on later cache hits. On any other error, delete the key.

findings.title: ProvideAnonDBStore signature change likely breaks the Wire dependency graph
findings.body:
Before this PR, `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` took an `anonstore.AnonStore` argument, so the Wire set (pkg/server/wire.go or the enterprise wireexts) must contain `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` plus a `wire.Bind` to `AnonStore`. That file is not in this PR.

`ProvideAnonDBStore` now needs an `int64`, which Wire cannot supply. If the provider stays in the set, code generation fails with either a missing int64 provider or an unused-provider error.

If another component still injects `anonstore.AnonStore`, it would get a second store instance that silently ignores the limit. Update or remove the Wire provider and binding in the same change.

findings.title: Limit keyed on a client-supplied header: trivially bypassed and abusable for lockout
findings.body:
Enforcement relies entirely on the `X-Grafana-Device-Id` header, which the client controls.

1. A request without the header returns nil from `TagDevice` and is authenticated anonymously. Unparseable IPs also return nil. So any non-browser client skips the limit entirely.
2. An unauthenticated attacker can send requests with random device IDs until `device_limit` is reached. Every new legitimate anonymous visitor is then rejected for up to 30 days, until rows age out of the `updated_at` window.

At minimum, document this behaviour. Ideally, rate-limit device creation or treat a missing device ID consistently with the limit.

findings.title: Check-then-insert lets concurrent requests exceed the device limit
findings.body:
`CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` and then a separate upsert, with no transaction or lock around them.

Concurrent first requests from different devices can all read `count < deviceLimit` and all insert. This is especially likely across multiple Grafana instances sharing the DB, or a burst of new visitors. The stored device count can therefore exceed the configured limit.

If the limit is meant as a hard cap, the count and insert need to be atomic, for example a conditional `INSERT ... SELECT` with a count predicate or a serialized transaction.

findings.title: Device tagging moved onto the synchronous auth path even when no limit is configured
findings.body:
Tagging used to run in a background goroutine with its own timeout and panic recovery. It now runs inline in `Authenticate` using the request context.

Every cache-miss anonymous request now waits for the DB upsert, plus a `COUNT(*)` when a limit is set, before it is authenticated. This applies even with the default `device_limit = 0`, where nothing needs to be enforced.

The panic recovery is also gone, and a client disconnect now cancels the write. Consider staying asynchronous when `AnonymousDeviceLimit == 0`.

findings.title: Tests don't cover existing devices at the limit or repeated requests from rejected devices
findings.body:
`TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only checks that a second new device is rejected.

It does not check that an already-registered device can still update once the limit is reached, which is the `updateDevice` path's main purpose. No test at the service or client level checks that a rejected device stays rejected on later requests, and such a test would have caught the local-cache bypass.

`Anonymous.Authenticate` returning an error on `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is also untested.

findings.title: anonymousDeviceLimit is inferred as type `undefined` on GrafanaBootConfig
findings.body:
`anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` has no type annotation, so TypeScript infers the property type as literal `undefined`, not `number | undefined`.

At runtime the backend sends a number, which is merged into the config. Code that reads `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` and treats it as a number, such as `config.anonymousDeviceLimit > 0`, will not type-check.

Declare it as `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;`.

findings.title: New device_limit setting not documented in defaults.ini/sample.ini or the docs
findings.body:
`[auth.anonymous] device_limit` is read here, but conf/defaults.ini, conf/sample.ini and the configuration docs are not updated.

Operators have no way to discover the option. Nothing tells them that exceeding it makes new anonymous visitors fail authentication.
